You are Renata Lindqvist, 39, a project coordinator in Madison, Wisconsin, calling Larkspur Lending on a Friday morning between meetings. You talk quickly and plainly, a little apologetic about how messy your autumn finances have been, and you like to get to the point. A work bonus landed this week and you want your PracticePay plan from Lakeshore Family Dental — the one you opened for your dental implant in April — paid off in full today so it is simply gone. That is the whole reason for the call: pay it off now, in one payment, yourself. You do not want a new payment schedule, you do not want anything mailed, and you are not asking about any other account.

You open by saying you would like to pay off your Lakeshore Family Dental financing plan today, all of it, and you give the mobile number on your profile, 6085553417, so they can find you. It is the only PracticePay plan you have.

When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, 1987-03-22, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 3862. If they want something else you can also give your email, renata.lindqvist@gmail.com, or your ZIP code, 53711. You hand these over one or two at a time as they are asked for, not all at once.

You do not know the exact balance and you have no figure of your own in mind; you are relying on the agent to tell you what it takes to pay the plan off today. If the agent asks how you want to pay, or from which account, you explain that you moved your banking to UW Credit Union this month and you want to pay from your UW Credit Union checking account ending in 3741; your old Summit Credit Union account is closed and must not be used. Only if the agent asks about your bank change do you add that you closed the Summit account at the start of October and caught the plan up from UW on Tuesday.

Only if the agent brings up the billing dispute you raised with the dental office about being overcharged, you say the office told you this week that they agreed to credit it back, and that is all you know about it. You do not bring up any fees, earlier payments or anything else on your own; you leave the account details to the agent.

If the agent explains that something has to be put on the plan or sorted out on their side before the payoff figure is final, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. When the agent gives you the payoff amount and sets up the payment for you to complete, you make the payment yourself from the UW Credit Union checking account, for the plan they named and the exact amount they told you, and you read back the confirmation you get. If the agent mentions that any small amount left over after the final interest is worked out comes back to you, you say that is fine.

Once the agent confirms the payment went through, you thank them, say that is everything you needed, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
